title: Switching from HL English Lit to LangLit in DP1
summary: Can you switch from HL English Literature to Language and Literature in DP1? Learn the rules, course differences, catch-up needs, and next steps.
body_markdown:
Yes, it may be possible to switch from **HL English A: Literature** to **HL English A: Language and Literature** during DP1. However, the change is not automatic and cannot be approved by the IB directly at a student's request. Your school must offer the course, approve the transfer, accommodate it within the timetable, and decide that you can realistically complete the missed learning.


The earlier in DP1 you ask, the more manageable the switch is likely to be. Before deciding, you need to understand that Language and Literature is not simply a less literary version of Literature. It includes substantial literary study but adds systematic analysis of non-literary texts, media, audiences, contexts, and communication.


### The short answer: your school decides whether you can switch


There is no universal IB rule guaranteeing students the right to change subjects during DP1. Equally, the IB's published regulations do not establish a general prohibition on moving between these two English A courses. In practice, subject-change policies, deadlines, class capacity, staffing, and timetabling are determined by individual schools.


Official assessment registration is handled through the school. The IB's[Diploma Programme general regulations](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/become-an-ib-school/pdfs/dp-2026-general-regulations.pdf) state that students cannot register themselves or amend an existing registration themselves. The **DP coordinator** manages this process, so that person must confirm what is possible in your circumstances.


A switch is most realistic when:


- You are still relatively early in DP1.
- HL Language and Literature is offered and has space.
- The two classes fit the same timetable block.
- You can catch up on the non-literary texts and concepts already taught.
- The receiving teacher supports the change.
- Your overall Diploma subject combination remains valid.


As explained in RevisionDojo's guide to[switching IB subjects during DP1 or DP2](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/can-i-change-subjects-in-the-middle-of-dp1-or-at-the-start-of-dp2-a-detailed-guide) , timing matters because missed content and assessment preparation accumulate quickly.


### How HL Literature and HL Language and Literature differ


Both subjects belong to the DP **studies in language and literature** group, and both develop close analysis, interpretation, argument, and academic writing. At HL, the IB recommends **240 teaching hours** for each course. Their assessment structures and weightings are similar, but the materials studied and the application of analytical skills are different.


Feature HL English A: Literature HL English A: Language and Literature


Main emphasis Literary works across forms, periods, cultures, and places Literary works plus non-literary texts and bodies of work


Minimum literary works **13 works** **6 works**


Non-literary study Not a formal course requirement A central course requirement


Paper 1 Analysis of two unseen literary passages Analysis of two unseen non-literary passages


Paper 2 Comparative essay on two studied literary works Comparative essay on two studied literary works


Individual Oral One work originally written in the language studied and one work studied in translation One literary work and one non-literary body of work


HL Essay Based on a studied literary work May be based on a studied literary work or non-literary body of work


The official[Language A: Literature course page](https://www.ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/curriculum/language-and-literature/language-a-literature/) confirms the larger literary reading requirement. The[Language A: Language and Literature course page](https://www.ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/curriculum/language-and-literature/language-a-language-and-literature/) explains that LangLit combines at least six literary works at HL with a wide range of non-literary texts and bodies of work.


This distinction affects how you read. Literature students concentrate almost entirely on literary form, style, structure, interpretation, and relationships among literary works. LangLit students apply related analytical principles to material such as speeches, advertisements, journalism, websites, photographs, campaigns, political cartoons, documentaries, and social media, depending on the teacher's course design.


RevisionDojo's[comparison of the Literature and Language and Literature curricula](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/what-is-the-ib-english-curriculum-a-complete-breakdown-of-literature-and-language-courses) provides a broader overview of these differences.


### What determines whether the switch will be approved?


### How much of DP1 has passed


A change after several weeks is normally easier than one near the end of DP1. By the middle or end of the year, the LangLit class may already have completed several non-literary bodies of work, practised Paper 1 repeatedly, and begun identifying options for the Individual Oral or HL Essay.


Late changes are not necessarily impossible, but the school must judge whether catch-up work is academically responsible. A desire to avoid a difficult unit is unlikely to be sufficient if the move creates a larger academic problem.


### Timetable, class size, and school policy


Even if the IB subject framework permits your combination, your school may be unable to make the change. The LangLit class could be full, taught in another timetable block, or unavailable at HL. Schools may also impose internal subject-change deadlines earlier than formal IB assessment registration deadlines.


Do not rely on another school's policy or another student's result. Ask your coordinator for your school's written policy and the exact date after which changes become restricted.


### Your reason for changing


A persuasive request explains why LangLit is a better academic fit. For example, you may be genuinely interested in rhetoric, journalism, advertising, political communication, visual media, or the relationship between language and power.


Be cautious if your only reason is that LangLit appears easier. Both are rigorous Language A courses assessed through analytical writing, comparison, oral argument, and independent coursework. LangLit involves fewer literary works, but it requires confident analysis across a broader range of text types.


### What would you need to catch up?


Your existing Literature skills will transfer. Close reading, thesis construction, analysis of authorial choices, paragraph development, and comparative writing remain valuable. Paper 2 is particularly familiar because both courses require a comparative essay on two literary works.


The largest gap is likely to be **non-literary analysis** . You may need to learn how to analyse:


- **Purpose and audience** , including how a text addresses particular groups.
- **Text type conventions** , such as the typical features of advertisements, speeches, articles, or campaigns.
- **Visual choices** , including composition, framing, colour, typography, gaze, and layout.
- **Rhetorical strategies** , such as appeals to authority, emotion, values, or shared identity.
- **Context and circulation** , including where, when, and through which medium a text appears.
- **Bodies of work** , meaning groups of non-literary texts connected through authorship, production, text type, campaign, or another defensible relationship.


Paper 1 requires particular attention. Under the official[Language and Literature subject brief](https://ibo.org/contentassets/5895a05412144fe890312bad52b17044/curriculum.brief-languagea.language.and.literature-eng.pdf) , HL students analyse two unseen non-literary passages in **2 hours 15 minutes** . Literature Paper 1 uses the same duration but presents literary material, as shown in the official[Literature subject brief](https://www.ibo.org/contentassets/5895a05412144fe890312bad52b17044/curriculum.brief-languagea.literature-eng.pdf) .


You must also establish which studied texts can count toward future assessments. A literary work studied in your Literature class does not automatically become part of the receiving teacher's LangLit course plan. The new teacher should identify what can transfer and what must be studied separately.


### How to decide whether switching is the right choice


Do not base the decision solely on your first grades. Early DP1 marks often reflect an adjustment to IB criteria rather than your eventual potential. Before requesting a transfer, compare the actual intellectual demands of both courses.


Ask yourself:


1. Do I prefer analysing only literature, or do I want to study media and everyday communication as well?
2. Am I interested in how audience, ideology, platform, and context shape language?
3. Am I willing to catch up independently without neglecting my other subjects?
4. Does either course better support my likely university plans?
5. Is the problem the course itself, or could feedback and improved technique resolve it?


Universities generally recognize both as rigorous English A subjects, but individual entry requirements vary. If you are considering English literature or another course with specific subject expectations, verify requirements on each university's official admissions page rather than assuming the two subjects are always treated identically.


### How to request the switch properly


Begin with the **DP coordinator** , not only the two English teachers. Explain your academic reason calmly and ask about the school's deadline, timetable, approval process, registration status, and effect on predicted grades.


Then meet the Language and Literature teacher and request a precise catch-up list covering:


- Literary works and non-literary bodies of work already studied.
- Concepts and terminology already introduced.
- Paper 1 tasks completed by the class.
- Current assessment planning.
- Notes, reading, and practice you must complete.
- A realistic deadline for demonstrating that you have caught up.


A useful proposal is a short written plan for the first four to six weeks after transferring. Complete targeted non-literary Paper 1 exercises, read any missed texts, and submit one diagnostic response for teacher feedback. RevisionDojo's[HL Language and Literature resources](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-english-langlit-new) and[Paper 1 practice area](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-english-langlit-new/ib-english-langlit-new-2-paper-1) can help you become familiar with non-literary analysis.


For writing development, use the[IB English assessment rubric guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-understand-and-apply-the-ib-english-assessment-rubrics) to check whether your argument, analysis, organization, and language meet the shared assessment expectations. Jojo AI can help diagnose a practice thesis or paragraph, but your teacher should confirm course-specific text choices and assessment eligibility.


### Conclusion


Switching from HL English Literature to HL English Language and Literature in DP1 is often possible, especially early in the year, but only your school can approve it. The decision should be based on academic fit rather than the assumption that LangLit is easier. Confirm the practical conditions, understand the non-literary catch-up required, and obtain a written plan from the receiving teacher before changing courses. If the transfer is approved, RevisionDojo's Study Notes, Questionbank, Paper 1 practice, and Jojo AI can help you close the initial skills gap systematically.
